subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the remaining fix changes public config and whether existing users see potentially important failed-mutation warnings after an apparently successful turn.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean path only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and close or narrow the final-only request to docs and channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split remaining leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle concrete channel or tool-class leaks such as Feishu aggregate failures or internal-warning routing in their own issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closest merged warning-policy fix and left this issue scoped as the broader delivery-policy decision.
